items.title: The structural comb-partition hypothesis
items.strategy: Define the uniform hypothesis on every complement-of-H-free ambient graph: each comb block splits into an F1-free part and a pure-blockade part whose pattern is F2-free and is pure to all other comb blocks. State the quantifiers explicitly, correcting the source's locally phrased restatement.

items.title: A large Y-part in a structural comb partition yields the clique-or-stable-set outcome
items.strategy: Choose a common Erdős–Hajnal exponent c in (0,1] for F1 and F2, lowering either exponent through positive-real power monotonicity. If some F1-free Y_i has size at least w/2, apply its exponent and use w at least 4 to prove (w/2)^c is at least w^(c/2) through the real-power definition and monotonicity.

items.title: A transversal of wide structural blocks yields the pure blockade outcome
items.strategy: From one block of size at least w/(2 ell) in each partition, use cross-block purity to make the selected blocks pairwise pure. Since ell is at least 4, their width is at least w/ell^2, which is the third property-(*) outcome.

items.title: Failure of the first and third property-(*) outcomes forces one small-block structural partition
items.strategy: If the homogeneous-set outcome fails, every Y_i has size below w/2 and hence every X_i has size at least w/2. If the pure-blockade outcome also fails, the transversal lemma supplies an index i for which every A_j^i has size at most w/(2 ell); summing then gives t_i at least ell.

items.title: Integral geometric layers of a decreasing block partition
items.strategy: For an ordered partition A_1,...,A_t with nonincreasing block sizes and ell at least 4, define the integral cutoff m_r as the largest index at most t and at most ell^(r/2). Define the layers by successive cutoff differences, stopping at the least q with m_q=t; no nonintegral index is used.

items.title: Integral geometric layers exist, cover the partition, and retain the required cutoff bounds
items.strategy: Prove the cutoff set has a largest integer and that a cutoff reaches t after finitely many steps. Establish ell^(r/4) at most m_r at most ell^(r/2), including the truncated terminal cutoff, and use the cutoff formula to prove strict increase and hence nonempty layers.

items.title: Homogeneous sets in pure-blockade patterns lift to complete or anticomplete blockades
items.strategy: Use the definition of the pattern graph: a clique of pattern vertices means every selected pair of blocks is complete, while a stable set means every selected pair is anticomplete. Preserve the selected blocks and their common width.

items.title: A wide integral geometric layer forces the complete-or-anticomplete property-(*) blockade
items.strategy: On the first m_r blocks, F2-freeness and its Erdős–Hajnal exponent give a pattern clique or stable set of size at least m_r^c. Lift it to the blocks. The rounded cutoff lower bound and c_2=10/c turn width w/ell^(5r/2) into at least w/k^(c_2), while k is at least ell^(c/4).

items.title: Successive small integral geometric layers contradict a large X-part
items.strategy: If every preterminal layer has a block below w/ell^(5r/2), monotonic block sizes bound the next layer by ell^((r+1)/2) w/ell^(5r/2). Add the initial layer bound w/(2 sqrt(ell)) and dominate the remaining finite sum by its geometric series; for ell at least 4 the total is strictly below w/2.

items.title: The structural comb-partition criterion implies property (*)
items.strategy: For the uniform structural hypothesis choose c_1=c_3=c/4 and c_2=10/c. Given a special-vertex comb, the large-Y lemma gives outcome one; otherwise failure of outcomes one and three yields a small-block partition, which is relabelled in nonincreasing size without changing its structural properties. A wide layer gives outcome two, and if none is wide the geometric-layer sum contradicts |X_i| at least w/2. This is a floor-safe repair of source Lemma 5.1.

title: The Structural Criterion for Property (*) — Examples

items.title: A large Y-part in a structural comb partition
items.strategy: Under the full structural comb-partition hypothesis, a common EH constant c=1/2, and a structurally partitioned (ell,16)-comb with ell>=4, a Y-part of size 8 meets w/2; apply the large-Y lemma to obtain its stated bound 16^(1/4)=2.

items.title: A wide transversal in four structural comb partitions
items.strategy: Give four selected blocks of size one in a four-tooth structural partition with w=8, list their pairwise complete-or-anticomplete adjacencies, and verify that they form a pure (4,1/2)-blockade.

items.title: Integral geometric layers for fourteen ordered blocks
items.strategy: For ell=4 and t=14, calculate the successive integral cutoffs 2,4,8,14 and the four layer sizes 2,2,4,6, showing explicitly how the final truncated layer replaces a nonintegral source index.

items.title: Omitting cross-block purity breaks the transversal conclusion
items.strategy: Specify four comb blocks whose selected pure-partition blocks include a mixed pair across two different comb blocks. The finite adjacency table shows that wide selected blocks alone do not form a pure transversal, so condition (2.3) is indispensable.
